entities.summary:
Francesco de Tatti was an Italian painter of the Renaissance period, active in Varese from 1512 to 1520.


Tatti's artistic output was limited, with only a handful of works attributed to him, but his style was influenced by the masters of the time, including Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo.


Despite his modest success, Tatti's work had a lasting impact on the development of Renaissance art, with his compositions reflecting the era's emphasis on humanism and classical ideals.


Tatti's legacy can be seen in the works of later artists, who drew inspiration from his innovative use of color and light.


One striking statistic about Tatti's work is that his most famous painting, 'The Madonna of the Rocks', has been the subject of intense scholarly debate over its authorship and dating.
